chapters.title: What a bank's technology actually is
chapters.dek: The machine behind the app: what a core banking system is, how anything else talks to it, and where the numbers on a customer's screen really come from.

chapters.title: The things that quietly kill deals
chapters.dek: Security, hosting and resilience. Three reviews you do not sit in, which decide whether your proposal survives the month after the good meeting.

chapters.title: How a bank actually buys
chapters.dek: Committees, calendars and budget cycles. Why the technically better answer loses to the one that arrives in the right quarter.

chapters.title: Holding your own in the room
chapters.dek: Diagrams, tenders and demos — the moments where a salesperson either becomes an advisor or gets handed back to procurement.

lessons.title: "Does it integrate with our existing system?"
lessons.dek: What an API actually is, why the answer is never yes or no, and how to turn the question that kills most deals into the one that scopes them.

lessons.title: Where the bank's data actually sits
lessons.dek: Live system, reporting copy, data warehouse. Three places the same number lives, three different truths, and the one a bank's analytics team is really asking you about.

lessons.title: The security review that quietly kills the deal
lessons.dek: Encryption, access control and Nghị định 13/2023 — in the words a Head of IT Security uses, and the four things to raise yourself before they ask.

lessons.title: Cloud, on-prem, or the thing in between
lessons.dek: Why a Vietnamese bank cannot simply move to AWS, what a hybrid answer looks like, and how hosting decides your price before anyone talks about features.

lessons.title: What happens when the other bank is down
lessons.dek: Queues, retries and the money that must not be lost or sent twice. The mechanism behind every "transfer is being processed" message a customer has ever seen.

lessons.title: Why the pilot took nine months
lessons.dek: Environments, UAT, change windows and the year-end freeze. Read a bank's delivery calendar and you will stop promising dates you cannot hold.

lessons.title: Who signs, and who can say no
lessons.dek: Procurement, the IT steering committee, the risk committee and your sponsor. Four people who can each stop the deal, only one of whom you have been talking to.

lessons.title: The budget cycle you are actually selling into
lessons.dek: Capex against opex, the annual plan, and why a deal that is obviously worth it still cannot be signed until March. Timing beats price more often than anyone admits.

lessons.title: Reading an architecture diagram in a meeting
lessons.dek: Every box, every arrow, and the three questions that make a bank's architect decide you are worth talking to. The lesson that ties the first three chapters together.

lessons.title: Reading an RFP without lying in it
lessons.dek: Mandatory against desirable, the compliance matrix, and how to answer "partially" in a way that scores points instead of disqualifying you.

lessons.title: The demo that survives a technical audience
lessons.dek: What to show, what never to show, and the three questions an architect asks to find out whether the product is real. Last, because it uses everything before it.
